articles.title: Acer Unveils Predator Atlas 8 Handheld PC
articles.summary: The Acer Predator Atlas 8 handheld PC boasts impressive graphics capabilities and lower price point compared to its closest rival.
articles.content: Acer's latest attempt to dominate the handheld PC market has arrived in the form of the Predator Atlas 8, which boasts impressive graphics capabilities at a significantly lower price point than its closest rival. The concept of modern handheld PCs began as a convenient solution for gamers on-the-go, allowing them to access their favorite titles without being tethered to a home console or powerful computer. However, as this category has evolved, manufacturers have pushed the boundaries of performance and design. A prime example of this trend is MSI's Claw 8 EX AI+, which boasts serious graphics power but comes with a hefty price tag of $1,800. In an effort to disrupt this status quo, Acer has unveiled the Predator Atlas 8, which features the same Intel Arc G3 Extreme chip as its more expensive counterpart. The result is a device that promises to deliver top-notch performance without breaking the bank, thanks in part to its aggressive pricing strategy. The question now is whether Acer's new offering can live up to its lofty claims and provide gamers with an alternative to the current framerate champion. The controller layout on the Predator Atlas 8 is reminiscent of Xbox consoles, featuring an Xbox-style button arrangement. However, some users may find the TMR analog sticks to be lacking in precision. For those who don't play fighting games or similar titles, the D-Pad is more than sufficient for navigating menus. One of the notable features of the Predator Atlas 8's controller is its rear paddles and shoulder buttons, which provide ample travel and are particularly useful for racing games. Additionally, the analog Hall-effect triggers offer a smooth gaming experience. The device also boasts a built-in fingerprint reader on the power button. Acer has equipped the Predator Atlas 8 with dual two-watt speakers that can produce surprisingly loud sound levels. However, when pushed to their limits (above 50 TK), these speakers tend to distort and produce an unpleasant crackly or crunchy effect. The audio quality is otherwise serviceable but may not be on par with other gaming devices. The overall design of the Predator Atlas 8's controller is fairly standard, though it does lack a USB-A port found on some competing models. This omission might be seen as a drawback for users who prefer to have multiple connectivity options at their disposal. The speakers on the Acer Predator Atlas 8 are remarkably punchy and clear, making it unnecessary to turn them up to high volumes even in loud environments. Unless you're planning a large gathering or event where music playback is crucial, the Atlas 8's audio capabilities may not be fully utilized. At its core, the handheld device boasts an Intel Arc G3 Extreme processor, identical to that found in the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, but with some key differences in storage and memory specifications. The performance of the Acer Predator Atlas 8 holds up remarkably well when compared to its counterparts in various gaming scenarios. When the device is set to run at lower power consumption levels - specifically 15 watts - it performs on par with the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+ in Returnal, a popular game that pushes graphics capabilities to the limit, delivering frame rates of 60 frames per second at FHD and medium graphics settings. The Atlas 8 offers seamless integration with Microsoft's Xbox experience, a dedicated gaming interface that allows for an immersive gaming experience without the clutter of a traditional desktop operating system. The battery life of the Predator Atlas 8 is quite impressive, allowing for extended gaming sessions without needing to be plugged in. In my testing, I was able to play World of Warcraft: Forever at FHD on medium settings for an hour and 45 minutes on a single charge while maintaining frame rates above 90. When switching to less demanding titles like Warhammer Survivors, the device's battery life increased significantly, lasting more than three hours before needing recharging. This suggests that the Predator Atlas 8 is capable of delivering long-lasting performance across various game genres and settings. The device's Balanced performance mode played a key role in these test results, allowing for optimal power consumption while still providing smooth gaming experiences. By tweaking this setting or experimenting with different modes, users may be able to further extend their untethered gaming sessions. For those willing to experiment with the Predator Atlas 8's settings, there is potential to optimize performance and battery life even further, making it an attractive option for mobile gaming enthusiasts seeking a balance between price, performance, and portability. The Acer Predator Atlas 8 offers impressive performance at a more affordable price point compared to its competitors. With a cost of $1,450, it is significantly cheaper than the MSI Claw 8 EX AI+, which shares the same processor but comes with a hefty price tag. While the device may lack some features, such as additional RAM and storage, its microSD card slot provides an alternative solution for expanding memory. The absence of a USB-A port and slightly less vibrant display are minor drawbacks, although the speakers' tendency to sound distorted at high volumes is a notable limitation. articles.title: Natalia Guzman introduces concept of smart aging in beauty industry
articles.summary: The beauty industry is shifting from antiaging to a more nuanced approach called "smart aging" that focuses on maintaining healthy skin while embracing the natural aging process.
articles.content: The beauty industry has seen significant changes in terminology over recent years, particularly when it comes to aging. Gone are the days of simply trying to reverse or halt the aging process altogether. Instead, a more nuanced approach is gaining traction. This shift away from antiaging reflects a growing understanding that aging is an inevitable and natural part of life. The latest buzzword, longevity, doesn't quite fill the gap for those seeking ways to maintain youthful-looking skin and bodies. However, there is a new concept emerging: smart aging. According to Natalia Guzman, FNP-C, CANS, a board-certified nurse practitioner at Atelier Aesthetix in Beverly Hills, this approach involves taking a proactive, science-based stance on maintaining healthy skin while embracing the natural aging process. Smart aging is not just about treating symptoms or trying to turn back the clock, but rather about making informed choices that support the skin's natural functions over time. As skin ages, its natural functions begin to slow down, leading to a decline in collagen production and cellular turnover. This gradual process is accelerated by environmental factors such as UV exposure, pollution, and lifestyle habits. As a result, visible signs of aging become apparent. The goal of smart aging is not to turn back the clock or eliminate these changes, but rather to address them strategically through preventative skin care and healthy lifestyle choices. When necessary, evidence-based aesthetic treatments can also be used to support the skin's natural functions over time. According to experts, the key difference between smart aging and traditional antiaging lies in its philosophy. For decades, the beauty industry has focused on fighting or erasing signs of aging, creating unrealistic expectations about looking younger indefinitely. Smart aging takes a more holistic approach, acknowledging that aging is a natural process that can be supported rather than prevented. This shift in perspective emphasizes the importance of investing in one's skin's future and being proactive about its health, rather than waiting until significant changes occur and trying to reverse them. By adopting this approach, individuals can take control of their skin's well-being and make informed choices that promote healthy aging. Aging well rather than fighting it is the core principle behind smart aging, a shift in focus from anti-aging to skin health and prevention. This approach encourages individuals to support their skin's natural evolution, rather than trying to eliminate wrinkles, fine lines, or changes in skin texture. By adopting this mindset, people can work with their skin's biology to help it function optimally for as long as possible. The goal is not to simply chase the appearance of youth but to prioritize skin quality, achieve natural-looking results, and maintain overall skin health. This approach recognizes that aging is a natural process that should be supported rather than resisted. The main difference between smart aging and traditional anti-aging methods is the emphasis on creating a long-term strategy for skin care. Rather than focusing solely on eliminating signs of aging, individuals can take steps to promote healthy aging through consistent skincare routines and healthy lifestyle habits. Daily broad-spectrum sunscreen with an SPF of at least 30 is a crucial component of this approach. Wearing sunscreen daily is the first step in a smart aging routine, according to experts who emphasize its importance in preventing premature skin aging caused by ultraviolet exposure. This simple yet effective habit can help individuals maintain healthy-looking skin and reduce their risk of wrinkles, loss of elasticity, and uneven pigmentation over time. To maintain healthy-looking skin and prevent long-term damage, experts recommend incorporating topical antioxidants into your skincare routine. Vitamin C, in particular, is beneficial for protecting against environmental oxidative stress that can lead to wrinkles, loss of elasticity, and uneven pigmentation over time. When it comes to choosing the right treatments, Guzman emphasizes the importance of selecting therapies tailored to an individual's specific needs. This means considering factors such as age, anatomy, and concerns when deciding on preventive or corrective aesthetic treatments like neuromodulators, collagen-stimulating injectables, microneedling, or energy-based devices. The goal is not to follow every new trend in the beauty industry but rather to choose treatments that address specific skin issues. By doing so, individuals can maintain or improve their skin's appearance without resorting to unnecessary or invasive procedures. Guzman stresses that this approach requires a deep understanding of each patient's unique requirements. In fact, prevention is key when it comes to maintaining healthy-looking skin over the long term. Experts agree that starting a smart aging routine early on, ideally in one's 20s, can have a significant impact on preventing premature signs of aging. The approach to skincare is shifting towards prevention over aggressive treatment, according to experts who advocate for smart aging. At 20 years old, individuals should prioritize establishing healthy habits that will benefit their skin in the long run, such as wearing sunscreen consistently and maintaining proper hydration. This stage is not about treating existing signs of aging but rather preventing them from occurring in the first place by introducing targeted active ingredients when necessary. As people enter their 30s, they may start to notice subtle changes in skin texture, fine lines, pigmentation, or elasticity, prompting a reassessment of their skincare routine and possibly considering professional treatments based on individual needs. Skin tone plays a significant role in determining the visible signs of aging, particularly for individuals with darker skin. Uneven pigmentation and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation can be more pronounced, making these concerns especially relevant when considering aesthetic treatments like lasers or chemical peels. These pigmentation issues are not only aesthetically concerning but also require thoughtful consideration when planning a skincare routine or undergoing professional treatments. Guzman emphasizes the importance of combining science, prevention, consistency, and aesthetic care in achieving healthy, youthful-looking skin. articles.summary: Millions of women in Afghanistan, particularly pregnant women, are suffering under Taliban restrictions and are increasingly losing access to life-saving medical care.

articles.title: Taliban Restrictions Limit Female Access to Medical Care in Afghanistan
articles.summary: A recent report by the United Nations details the struggles faced by women in Taliban-ruled territories who are being denied medical care due to stringent rules and reduced international aid funding.
articles.content: In Afghanistan's Taliban-ruled territories, a new reality has emerged where male doctors are barred from treating women. The drastic measure has been documented in a recent report by the United Nations, which paints a grim picture of the struggles faced by women. A harrowing case from Kunar province illustrates the dire consequences: a woman suffered multiple miscarriages due to her inability to access medical care. This is not an isolated incident; it highlights the alarming trend of pregnant women who desperately need medical attention but are being denied treatment because of the Taliban's restrictions. The escalating crisis is fueled by two main factors: the Taliban's stringent rules and the significant reduction in international aid funding for healthcare services. As a result, women in Afghanistan are increasingly losing access to essential medical care. Tamana Zaryab Paryani, a 28-year-old Afghan women's rights activist, has spoken out against the regime. Her words carry weight due to her unwavering commitment to fighting for women's rights and her experience as a vocal critic of the Taliban. The Taliban's restrictive policies have had a devastating impact on Afghan women, limiting their access to education, employment, and healthcare. Paryani's message to the international community is clear: she expects them to recognize the systematic disenfranchisement of women in Afghanistan as gender apartheid and take action to support them. Her words carry significant weight due to her unwavering commitment to fighting for women's rights and her experience as a vocal critic of the Taliban. The UN Assistance Mission in Afghanistan has been monitoring the human rights situation in the country, documenting the severe restrictions imposed on women by the Taliban. In September 2025, they reported that inspectors from the Ministry for the Promotion of Virtue and Prevention of Vice were further limiting women's access to healthcare through regulations and decrees. The consequences of these restrictions are dire: around 2.6 million girls are excluded from secondary education, which can lead to increased child marriage and maternal mortality rates. The UN Women organization has sounded the alarm on this issue, warning that it will have far-reaching effects on Afghan women's lives. The Taliban's decrees have been relentless since their return to power in 2021, severely restricting women's opportunities for work outside the home and denying them access to universities. Girls are barred from secondary education, forcing many to resort to secret studies to continue their education. Afghanistan's population is predominantly young, with approximately 42% below the age of 15. This demographic profile contributes to the country's pressing health challenges, particularly in addressing the nutritional needs of its children and pregnant women. The systematic oppression of Afghan women has been described by Haroon Mutasem, a professor of International Criminal Law at the American University of Afghanistan, as an institutionalized system of domination. According to Mutasem, this system denies women equal rights and opportunities, relegating them to secondary status in society. Mutasem explains that women are often viewed as being responsible for domestic duties, including childcare and meeting the sexual needs of their husbands. This narrow definition of a woman's role is deeply ingrained in Afghan culture and perpetuated by the country's patriarchal laws and institutions. The UN estimates that by 2027, more than 4 million children under five will require treatment for acute malnutrition. Additionally, around 1.27 million pregnant and breastfeeding women will also need care due to their vulnerability to malnutrition. Mutasem warns that if the international community fails to address the systematic oppression of Afghan women, it could undermine the universal validity of human rights. He cautions that other authoritarian regimes and extremist movements may adopt similar practices, further eroding the protections afforded by international law. Afghanistan is currently facing its worst women's rights crisis, according to Susan Ferguson, the UN's Special Representative in Afghanistan. The situation has reached a critical point where Afghan women are fighting for their very survival, as stated by Ferguson. Humanitarian organisations are being forced to make impossible decisions about which women and girls can receive support due to cuts in aid funding. This means that many women are being turned away from receiving the help they desperately need, exacerbating an already dire situation. articles.title: Migrant Arrivals Reach 1,990 on Canary Islands
articles.summary: A record number of migrants arrived at the Canary Islands on Tuesday, putting a strain on resources as authorities struggle to provide support.
articles.content: Spanish authorities have confirmed that nearly 2,000 migrants arrived at the Canary Islands on Tuesday, marking a significant milestone in the number of migrant arrivals to the archipelago. The influx of migrants has come just before Spain's national election later this week, when migration is expected to be a major concern for many voters. The islands' location off the coast of West Africa makes them a key entry point for migrants attempting to reach Europe. A record 1,990 people arrived on Tuesday, with search and rescue vessels accompanying multiple dinghies to the small island of El Hierro. This surge in arrivals has put a strain on resources, as authorities struggle to provide adequate support to those in need. Among the arrivals were around 100 minors, including a four-day-old baby that was born during the journey. Regional leader Fernando Clavijo expressed concern about the situation, describing Tuesday's events as "a historic day. The Canary Islands have long been a popular destination for tourists drawn by their mild climate, but they also serve as a key entry point for migrants desperate to reach Europe. The Canary Islands' population is being stretched to its limits as a record number of migrants continue to arrive on the islands. Over 26,000 people have reached the archipelago this year alone, and the numbers show no signs of slowing down. One of the main reasons for the surge in arrivals is the favorable sailing conditions that have prevailed in recent weeks. The calm seas have made it easier for boats to set sail from West Africa, where many migrants are desperate to escape poverty and find work. As a result, November has seen a significant spike in numbers, with half of this year's total arriving during the month. The Canary Islands' location makes them an attractive destination for migrants seeking to reach Europe, but it also puts a strain on local resources. Many of those who arrive are exhausted and in poor condition, requiring medical attention and other forms of support. Clavijo, the local official, has expressed his concern about the island's ability to cope with such large numbers. Clavijo pointed out that most of the boats arriving on Tuesday were from Senegal and Gambia, two countries where economic opportunities are scarce. Despite efforts by the European Union to reduce migration from West Africa, many people see leaving as their only option for a better life. As Clavijo noted, these people looking for a better future ended up on our shores. The situation is particularly challenging in El Hierro, the western-most island of the archipelago, which has a population of just 12,000. Clavijo expressed his satisfaction with the transfer of adult migrants to mainland Spain but acknowledged that help was needed to care for unaccompanied minors who require special attention from authorities. The Canary Island leader has spoken out against xenophobic rhetoric used by some politicians in Spain's election campaign. Clavijo, a member of the regional Canary Coalition party, criticized those who seek to demonize migrants, labeling such discourse as a xenophobic approach from individuals with questionable intentions. This sentiment was echoed by his stance on international agreements related to migrant relocation. He dismissed the recent deal between Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece, and the Netherlands to send migrants to Rwanda as preposterous." The regional leader's comments come ahead of Spain's elections, where the conservative Popular Party is vying for power against the ruling Socialist-led government. The Popular Party has been campaigning on a platform that includes stricter migrant policies, potentially requiring an alliance with the far-right Vox party to form a new government. articles.title: Ethiopian Troops and Allies Accused of War Crimes in Tigray
articles.summary: Amnesty International is calling for an independent investigation into possible war crimes committed by Ethiopian troops and their allied militia in Tigray after verifying 14 civilian deaths.
articles.content: Amnesty International has called for an independent investigation into possible war crimes committed by Ethiopian troops and their allied militia in Tigray. The human rights organization made this demand after verifying 14 civilian deaths in four artillery attacks on Alamata between September 26-28. Eyewitness accounts from residents near the Eritrean border paint a picture of military buildups and fears of another war. In particular, the town of Alitena in Tigray's Irob district is said to be bracing for potential conflict with neighboring Eritrea. Berhe Sibagadis, a 41-year-old father of four who lives there, is preparing to relocate his family further from the border. Amnesty International based its findings on interviews with residents, including survivors and medical personnel, as well as an analysis of videos, photographs, and satellite imagery. The organization accused forces allied with the Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) of putting civilians at risk by establishing military positions in residential areas and schools. The TPLF has rejected these allegations in a written response to Amnesty International. Meanwhile, the Ethiopian government and military have not commented on the report, nor did they respond before its publication. This lack of response from authorities has raised further concerns about the human rights situation in Tigray. Amid renewed fighting in Tigray and growing fears of a wider conflict between Ethiopia and Eritrea, Amnesty International's call for an independent investigation into possible war crimes takes on added urgency. The organization's findings highlight the need for accountability and transparency in the region. Fears of an impending conflict are running high among residents of Irob, a region in Ethiopia's Tigray province, where Eritrean forces have been spotted moving military equipment and personnel. Local residents report seeing tanks and heavy weapons being transported to the border area, while others describe digging fortifications that suggest preparations for war. Hagos Niguse, an Irob resident, said he has witnessed firsthand the buildup of Eritrean troops in his area. He claims to have seen them moving equipment and supplies towards the border with Tigray. The presence of Eritrean forces has left many residents feeling uneasy and vulnerable. Yonas Desta, a resident of Rama, described the military movements he has observed in his area. He said drones have been hovering overhead, while artillery fire and direct clashes between Ethiopian and Eritrean forces have been reported. Residents are living in fear of what might happen next, with many wondering if war is indeed imminent. The presence of Eritrean troops alongside TPLF fighters has raised concerns about the potential for renewed conflict in the region. According to local residents, the two groups were positioned together during the 2020-2022 war against Ethiopian forces. However, it remains unclear whether this alliance still exists or if new tensions have arisen. The situation on the ground remains tense and volatile, with both sides preparing for what appears to be an impending conflict. The fears of local residents are echoed by human rights groups and U.N. experts who have accused Eritrean troops of wartime abuses during the 2020-2022 war. A recent escalation in tensions between Ethiopia and Eritrea has raised concerns about a potential military confrontation along the Badme front. According to ACLED's senior analyst for East Africa, Jalale Getachew Birru, the risk of a full-scale conflict is now high, with Ethiopian troops massing nearby as Eritrean reinforcements re-entered the area around November 15. Badme was a key battleground in the border war between Ethiopia and Eritrea from 1998 to 2000, which claimed an estimated 70,000 lives according to the U.N. peacekeeping mission that followed. The region's volatile history has led to ongoing tensions between Addis Ababa and Asmara, particularly over claims of Eritrean support for Tigrayan rebels in Ethiopia.
